mainTopic: The light impurity of עליון של זב and of a בועל נדה's bed, and the משנה's reasons why כותים men count as בועלי נדות.
overview: The amud first finishes reading the פסוק about a זב. 'What is under him' cannot mean the bed beneath the זב, because another פסוק already teaches that. So it must mean something lying on top of him, עליון של זב, and the word 'והנשא' adds something he carries. The Torah lowered these to a light impurity that affects only food and drink, and the word 'יטמא' shows this. Next, a ברייתא on ויקרא 15:24 shows from 'יטמא שבעת ימים' that a בועל נדה is impure for a full seven days of his own, and learns from 'ותהי נדתה עליו' that he makes people and clay vessels impure like her. His bed, however, is lowered to a light impurity because the phrase about it is extra. אביי and רבא each explain why the פסוק is not read as a כלל ופרט, and רבא shows that the word 'עליו' makes the comparison work only in the strict direction. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about כותים. It limits it to married men and brings two explanations of how כותים women count their days wrongly. This leads to a debate over whether part of a day counts as a whole day for זיבה. The amud ends with רמי בר חמא asking whether a woman who discharges semen cancels a day of her count.

steps.title: The verse cannot mean the bed under the זב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects reading 'תחתיו' as the bed beneath the זב, because a different פסוק already teaches that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'under him' means a bed under the זב, that is already learned from 'And whoever touches his bed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one way to read the word 'תחתיו' (under him) and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a bed under a זב (משכב) is impure is already taught in ויקרא 15:5. If our פסוק meant the same thing, it would be saying something we already know. So 'תחתיו' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offering a possible reading in order to test it)
A man with an unusual discharge, who is a source of impurity
Something a זב lies on, which becomes a strong source of impurity
It is derived from (that source already)

phrases.english: If you say it means what is beneath the zav —
that is already derived from 'And whoever touches his bed'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of ויקרא 15:10 from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'תחתיו' as the bed beneath the זב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would repeat what ויקרא 15:5 already teaches.

steps.title: The verse means bedding above the זב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the פסוק as 'anything the זב will be under', which means bedding on top of the זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: whoever touches anything that the זב will be under. What is that? Bedding above the זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading: the פסוק is talking about something on top of the זב, called עליון של זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are read so that the זב is under the item, not the item under the זב. This gives the פסוק a new teaching, so it is no longer a repeat of 15:5.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (bringing in the correct reading)
Something lying on top of a זב, like a blanket
And what is it? (asks for the specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: 'תחתיו' in this פסוק means the זב is under the item, so it is talking about עליון של זב.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'under him' as the item being under the זב. Here the זב is the one underneath.

phrases.english: Rather: one who touches anything
that the zav will be under,
and what is that? What is above the zav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא הנוגע בכל אשר יהיה הזב תחתיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after step 1 rejected the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תחתיו means bedding above the זב (עליון של זב).

steps.title: Something carried by the זב is also impure
steps.stepSummary: The word 'והנושא' is read to teach that something the זב carries is also impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the one who carries' is also impure. What is that? Something carried by the זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second case from the same פסוק: an item the זב carries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word normally means a person who carries something. Here it is read as an object being carried by the זב. That object is like עליון של זב, because the זב is under it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the one who carries
Something that is carried (by the זב)
Also

phrases.english: 'And the one who carries' also becomes impure,
and what is that? Something carried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to the עליון של זב from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item carried by a זב is impure, like עליון של זב.

steps.title: How do we know it means the carried item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the פסוק shows that it means the carried item.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the reading in step 3. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual meaning of 'הנושא' is the person who carries. So the גמרא needs to show how the words of the פסוק allow reading it as the thing being carried.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason / source?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק shows that it means the item carried by the זב.

steps.title: The verse is written as 'והנשא'
steps.stepSummary: The way the word is written in the פסוק allows reading it as 'the thing carried'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'והנשא'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the written form of the word can be read as 'the carried thing'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is written without a ו, so it can be read נִשָּׂא, meaning something that is carried. That reading supports step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: And the thing that is carried
It is written

phrases.english: 'And the carried thing' is written.
phrases.notes: Since it's written without a ו, the letters can be read as 'the thing being carried' instead of 'the one who carries.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word is written so that it can be read נִשָּׂא, the thing carried.

steps.title: The verse lowered it to a light impurity
steps.stepSummary: The Torah moved עליון של זב away from the strict impurity of a משכב, so it makes only food and drink impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse took it out of the strict impurity and put it into a light impurity. This tells you it makes only food and drink impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the practical result: עליון של זב is only a light impurity that affects food and drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bed under a זב is a strong impurity (טומאה חמורה). The Torah wrote the עליון case separately with a lighter rule. That shows it does not make people or clothes impure, only אוכלין ומשקין.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse separated it (from another category)
Strict impurity
Light impurity
Food and drink

steps.whatToRemember: עליון של זב makes only food and drink impure, not people or clothes.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same source, a זב, can create different levels of impurity depending on whether the item is under him or on top of him.

phrases.english: The verse removed it from strict impurity,
and brought it to light impurity,
to tell you that it does not make impure
anything except food and drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the halachic result of the cases identified in steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עליון של זב makes only אוכלין ומשקין impure.

steps.title: Maybe it is only slightly less strict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps it is only a bit lighter, and still makes people and clothes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the verse removed it from strict impurity only in that it does not make a person impure enough for him to make his clothes impure. But it should still make a person or clothes impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 6. Maybe the impurity was lowered only one level, not all the way down to food and drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משכב makes a person impure, and he also makes his clothes impure. Maybe the Torah only removed that extra stage. Then עליון של זב would still make the person or clothes themselves impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (perhaps it means something else)
To make clothes impure
Let it make impure

phrases.english: Say the verse removed it from strict impurity
in that it does not make a person impure enough to make clothes impure,
but let it still make a person or clothes impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far step 6 lowered the impurity.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that it makes only food and drink impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being 'removed from strict impurity' could mean a small reduction, not a full drop to food and drink.

steps.title: The word 'יטמא' points to light impurity
steps.stepSummary: The word 'יטמא' itself shows a light impurity, so it affects only food and drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'יטמא', which means a light impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses 'יטמא' by itself and does not say anything about washing clothes. The גמרא reads this as pointing to טומאה קלה. So the full drop to food and drink stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Will be impure
It implies

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'יטמא' shows that עליון של זב carries only a light impurity, which affects food and drink.

phrases.english: The verse says 'will be impure',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:10

phrases.english: which implies light impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is only slightly lighter and still makes people and clothes impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יטמא' implies טומאה קלה, so it affects only food and drink.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the bedding under a בועל נדה is impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the bedding beneath a man who was with a נדה becomes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the bedding underneath a man who was with a נדה, from where do we know it is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants the source that the bedding under a בועל נדה is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this dealt with the upper layer of a זב, the עליון של זב. Now the גמרא turns to a different case, the bedding beneath a בועל נדה, and asks which פסוק teaches that it is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The bedding or item underneath him
A man who had relations with a woman who is a נדה
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And the bedding beneath one who was with a נדה, from where do we know it is impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the עליון של זב discussion to a new case from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source for the impurity of the bedding under a בועל נדה.

steps.title: A ברייתא begins with the words 'and her impurity be upon him'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא that starts from the phrase 'ותהי נדתה עליו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And her impurity be upon him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by quoting a ברייתא. This line only opens the ברייתא, and the rest of it is explained in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא starts from a phrase that seems to say he takes on her impurity. The ברייתא now has to work out what exactly carries over from her to him. The actual answer about his bedding comes at the end of this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And her impurity be upon him'

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'And her impurity be upon him,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a ברייתא built on ויקרא 15:24, starting from 'ותהי נדתה עליו'.

steps.title: Maybe he just follows her count of days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that 'her impurity upon him' might mean he finishes his impurity whenever she finishes hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he goes up with her, finishing his impurity on the same day she does.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible wrong reading of the phrase. Maybe he simply joins her schedule and becomes pure when she does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'her impurity is upon him' means he copies her status exactly, then a man who was with her late in her days would become pure early, together with her. The ברייתא raises this idea so that it can reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (an idea the ברייתא raises in order to reject it)
He goes up with her, counting by her days

phrases.english: One might think he goes up according to her timing?
phrases.notes: So if he was with her on her sixth day, he would become pure along with her the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible meaning of the phrase quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he takes on her impurity, perhaps he also takes on her remaining days and no more.

steps.title: No, he is impure for a full seven days
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'he shall be impure seven days', so he counts a full seven days of his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He shall be impure seven days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea from step 11. The פסוק clearly gives him a full seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק spells out seven days for him. So he does not finish together with her. He counts a full seven days from when he was with her.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says (introduces the proof from the פסוק)
Seven days

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: 'He shall be impure seven days.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possibility raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explicit wording in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He becomes pure when she does.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is impure for a full seven days of his own.

steps.title: Then what does 'her impurity upon him' teach?
steps.stepSummary: Since the phrase does not teach the timing, the ברייתא asks what it does teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what does the פסוק come to teach with 'and her impurity be upon him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks what the phrase is for now that it does not mean he follows her days. This step sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every phrase in the Torah must teach something. Since step 12 ruled out the timing idea, the phrase still needs a job.

keyTerms.meaning: So what does the פסוק come to teach?

phrases.english: Then what does the verse teach by saying 'And her impurity be upon him'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 12 removing the first possible meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the phrase 'ותהי נדתה עליו' teaches.

steps.title: Like her, he makes people and clay vessels impure
steps.stepSummary: The phrase teaches that the בועל נדה makes people and clay vessels impure, just as she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought he does not make people and clay vessels impure. So the פסוק says 'her impurity is upon him': just as she makes people and clay vessels impure, so does he.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 13. The phrase compares him to her: like her, he makes people and clay vessels impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase does not give him her timing. Instead, it gives him her power to make things impure. So a person or a clay vessel that he makes impure becomes impure, just as it would from her.

keyTerms.meaning: A clay or earthenware vessel
Just as she, so too he (a comparison)

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֹא יְטַמֵּא אָדָם וּכְלִי חֶרֶס,
phrases.english: For one might think he does not make a person and a clay vessel impure,
therefore the verse says 'And her impurity be upon him':

phrases.aramaic: מָה הִיא מְטַמְּאָה אָדָם וּכְלִי חֶרֶס,
phrases.english: just as she makes a person and a clay vessel impure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא מְטַמֵּא אָדָם וּכְלִי חֶרֶס.
phrases.english: so too he makes a person and a clay vessel impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֹא יְטַמֵּא אָדָם וּכְלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase compares him to her, so he makes people and clay vessels impure just as she does.

steps.title: Then maybe his bedding is as strongly impure as hers
steps.stepSummary: If he is compared to her, maybe his bedding and seat also carry her strong impurity, reaching a person and that person's clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as she makes a bed and seat impure enough to make a person impure and his clothes impure, maybe he does the same?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes the comparison further. If he is like her, maybe what he lies or sits on is as strongly impure as what she lies or sits on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her bed and seat become a full משכב and מושב, which makes a person who touches it impure, together with the clothes he is wearing. The challenge is that the comparison might carry over this strong power too.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then just as (pushing a comparison further)
Something lain on and something sat on, which can become strongly impure
Clothes

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה הִיא עוֹשָׂה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב
phrases.english: If so, just as she makes a bed and a seat impure
to make a person impure, and to make his clothes impure,
so too he would make a bed and a seat impure
to make a person impure, and to make his clothes impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה הִיא עוֹשָׂה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the comparison of step 14 to his bedding.
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the comparison between him and her goes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he matches her impurity, his bedding should match hers in strength as well.

steps.title: His bedding is impure, but only in a lighter way
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק simply says his bed 'shall be impure', which shows a lighter impurity than her משכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And every bed he lies on shall be impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the challenge from step 15. This same line also answers the opening question of step 9: his bedding is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא answers the challenge by quoting the separate phrase about his bed. Step 17 explains why this phrase limits him: 'ותהי נדתה עליו' already covered his bed, so the extra phrase must be there to lower its level. So his bedding is impure, but it does not make a person and his clothes impure the way her bedding does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall be impure', the plain wording that points to a lighter impurity

steps.whatToRemember: A בועל נדה is impure for seven days, and like her he makes people and clay vessels impure. His bedding is impure, but only lightly, unlike her strong משכב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'ותהי נדתה עליו' makes him equal to her in everything. He matches her in some ways, like making people and clay vessels impure, but not in her timing or in the strength of her bedding.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's rule about the bedding under כותים, who are treated as men who were with a נדה.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: 'And every bed
that he lies upon shall be impure.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:24

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר וְכׇל הַמִּשְׁכָּב אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב עָלָיו יִטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 15 and completes the answer to step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise wording of the פסוק limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His bedding is as strongly impure as hers.
steps.terutzMaskana: His bedding is impure, but only with a lighter impurity, because the phrase about his bed is extra (step 17).

steps.title: The extra phrase about his bed lowers its impurity to food and drink only
steps.stepSummary: Since 'ותהי נדתה עליו' already makes his bed impure, the extra phrase must be teaching that his bed has only a light impurity, affecting just food and drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was no need for the פסוק to say 'and every bed he lies on shall be impure.' So why does it say it? The פסוק took him out of the severe impurity and put him into a light impurity. It teaches that his bed makes only food and drinks impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing its answer from step 16 and shows how it learns it: the phrase about his bed is extra, so it must be teaching something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ותהי נדתה עליו' already compares him to a נדה, so his bed would be impure anyway. Since the Torah still adds 'every bed he lies on shall be impure,' that phrase must come to set his bed apart from her severe level. The result is that his bed makes only food and drinks impure, and not people or clothes.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק needs to say (here: 'there is no need for the פסוק to say')
The פסוק separated him (from her law)
Severe impurity (the level of the נדה's own bed)
Light impurity
Food and drinks, which can become impure even from a weak level of impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Both the man himself and his bed are being discussed. The man is like her (he makes people and clay vessels impure, step 14), but his BED is weaker than her bed.

phrases.english: For there is no need for the פסוק to say
'And every bed upon which he lies shall be impure',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:24. It's extra because 'her impurity is upon him' already covers his bed.

phrases.english: so why does the פסוק say
'And every bed upon which, etc.'?
The פסוק separated him from the severe impurity
and brought him to a light impurity,
to tell you that it makes impure
only food and drinks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the answer in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra phrase in the פסוק teaches a limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His bed would carry her severe impurity, reaching a person and that person's clothes.
steps.terutzMaskana: His bed is lowered to a light impurity that makes only food and drinks impure.

steps.title: רב אחאי: maybe the lowering is smaller
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי suggests 'light' may only mean his bed can't make a person impure who then makes his clothes impure. It could still make a person or clothes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי challenges: Say the פסוק took him out of the severe impurity and put him into a lighter one only in this way: his bed does not make a person impure so that the person makes clothes impure. But let it still make a person or clothes impure!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי questions how far the 'lighter impurity' goes. Maybe it is only one step lighter, not all the way down to food and drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her bed is very strong: a person who touches it becomes impure, and so do the clothes he is wearing. רב אחאי says the פסוק may only remove that extra chain to the clothes. His bed could still make a person or clothes impure directly, which is less than the ברייתא's 'only food and drinks.'

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges / refutes
Say instead (suggests another reading)
A person who then makes clothes impure

phrases.english: Rav Achai challenges:
Say that the פסוק separated him from the severe impurity
and brought him to a light impurity
meaning it does not make a person impure so that he makes clothes impure,
but let it make a person or clothes impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the lowering in step 17 goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that his bed makes only food and drinks impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Lighter' could mean only one step down from her level, leaving it still able to make people and clothes impure.

steps.title: רב אסי: the word 'יטמא' means a light impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that the wording 'shall be impure' itself points to a light impurity, all the way down to food and drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: 'shall be impure' means a light impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers רב אחאי by pointing to the exact word the Torah uses for his bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah just says 'יטמא', 'it shall be impure,' with no mention of making a person or clothes impure. That plain wording shows the lowest level of impurity. So the ברייתא is right: his bed affects only food and drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall be impure
It implies / means

steps.whatToRemember: His bed has only a light impurity: it makes food and drinks impure, not people or clothes.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
'Shall be impure' means a light impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחאי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His bed might still make a person or clothes impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'יטמא' shows the lightest impurity, food and drinks only.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק is a general statement limited by a detail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'ותהי נדתה עליו' is a general rule and 'וכל המשכב' is the detail, so the comparison to her would cover only bed and seat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'And her impurity is upon him' is a general statement. 'And every bed' is a detail. With a general statement followed by a detail, the general statement includes only what is in the detail. So bed and seat, yes; anything else, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge using the rule of כלל ופרט, which would shrink the comparison between him and the נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under כלל ופרט, the general phrase is limited to the detail that follows it. Then 'her impurity is upon him' would only mean that his bed and seat are impure. That would undo step 14, which learned that he makes people and clay vessels impure just like her.

keyTerms.meaning: A general statement in a פסוק
A specific detail in a פסוק
A rule for reading פסוקים: a general statement followed by a detail covers only the detail
Bed and seat
Anything else

phrases.english: Say: 'And her impurity is upon him' is a general statement,
'and every bed' is a detail,
and with a general statement and a detail,
the general statement includes only what is in the detail,
so bed and seat, yes,
anything else, no!
phrases.notes: So he would no longer make people and clay vessels impure like her, as step 14 taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge, this time against the comparison to her in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that the בועל נדה makes people and clay vessels impure like her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the פסוק as כלל ופרט would limit 'her impurity is upon him' to bed and seat only.

steps.title: אביי: the general statement and detail are too far apart
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that 'he shall be impure seven days' stands between the two parts, so they are not read as a כלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'He shall be impure seven days' breaks up the topic. So it is a general statement and a detail that are far from each other. Any general statement and detail that are far from each other are not read by the rule of כלל ופרט.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by showing that the rule of כלל ופרט does not apply to this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads: 'her impurity is upon him, he shall be impure seven days, and every bed...' The middle phrase separates the general statement from the detail. When they are separated like this, the detail does not limit the general statement, so the full comparison to her stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaks up the topic
That are far from each other
We do not learn / apply

steps.whatToRemember: The בועל נדה makes people and clay vessels impure like her, but his bed has only a light impurity. The פסוק is not read as כלל ופרט because its parts are separated.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps both teachings of the ברייתא: the full comparison to her (step 14) and the lighter impurity of his bed (step 17).

phrases.english: Abaye said:
'He shall be impure seven days' breaks up the topic,
phrases.notes: In ויקרא 15:24 this phrase comes right between 'her impurity is upon him' and 'every bed.'

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵי כְּלָל וּפְרָט הַמְרוּחָקִין זֶה מִזֶּה,
phrases.english: so it is a general statement and a detail that are far from each other,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל כְּלָל וּפְרָט הַמְרוּחָקִין זֶה מִזֶּה
phrases.english: and any general statement and detail that are far from each other,
we do not read it by the rule of general statement and detail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כלל ופרט challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The reading rule does not apply here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is a כלל ופרט, limiting him to bed and seat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The parts are separated, so no כלל ופרט; the full comparison to her stands.

steps.title: רבא: The word 'and every' widens the rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the כלל ופרט challenge differently from אביי. Even if a כלל ופרט can be far apart, the word 'וכל' is a ריבוי, which widens the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Really, we do learn from a general rule and a detail even when they are far apart. But the word 'and every' is a word that widens the rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the challenge from Step 20. He explains why the comparison to her is not limited to just bed and seat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the words in between break up the כלל ופרט. רבא agrees that a כלל ופרט can work even when far apart. He says this verse is still not a כלל ופרט, because the word 'וכל' (and every) is a ריבוי that widens the rule instead of narrowing it. So the comparison 'ותהי נדתה עליו' stays wide and is not cut down to bed and seat only.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (I hold the opposite of what was just said)
We derive, we learn out (a rule)
A widening word; a word in the פסוק that adds more cases
And every; a word that widens the rule

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with the result of אביי. Both agree the comparison is not limited to bed and seat. They only give different reasons.

phrases.english: Rava says: Actually, we do derive [from a far-apart general rule and detail],
phrases.notes: Unlike אביי, he holds that a כלל ופרט still works even when other words stand in between.

phrases.english: [but] "and every" is an amplification.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:24, 'וכל המשכב': 'and every bed'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same challenge that אביי answered in Step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the verse: the detail is really a widening word, so there is no כלל ופרט
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to her would be limited to bed and seat because of the כלל ופרט
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וכל' widens the rule, so the comparison to her stays broad

steps.title: רבי יעקב: Maybe his touch and bedding should both be lenient
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב argues that if he is compared to her, the comparison should go all the way. For her, touch and bedding are treated the same. So for him too, touch and bedding should be treated the same, which here means both lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב challenges: Say he is like her. With her, you made no difference between her touch and her bedding when it comes to making a person and his clothes impure; both are strict. So too with him, make no difference between his touch and his bedding; both should be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב challenges the idea that the man's touch is strict while his bedding is lenient. He uses the comparison to her to argue that both should be the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps showed that his bedding has only a light impurity. רבי יעקב asks: the comparison to her teaches that touch and bedding go together, so why not make his touch light too? For her both are strict. For him, since the bedding is clearly light, the touch should be light as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges, raises a strong objection
Touch; impurity passed on by touching
Bedding; something lain on, which can become impure
On the strict side
On the lenient side

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov objects to this:
Say [he is] like her,
just as with her, you did not differentiate
between her touch and her bedding,
to make a person impure and to make clothes impure, for stringency,
so too with him, do not differentiate
between his touch and his bedding,
to make a person impure and to make clothes impure, for leniency!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב: אֵימָא כְּהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the broad comparison to her goes, now that רבא has kept it broad
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that his touch is strict while his bedding is lenient
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison to her means touch and bedding are treated alike. Since his bedding is lenient, his touch should be lenient too.

steps.title: רבא: 'Upon him' means a heavy rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the word 'עליו' (upon him) means the Torah wants to put a weight on him. So the comparison works only in the strict direction, and his touch stays strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: 'Upon him' means to put a burden on him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבי יעקב by pointing to one word in the פסוק. That word shows the comparison to her is meant to be strict, not lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ותהי נדתה עליו' says her impurity is 'upon him,' like a load placed on him. So we may compare him to her only to make things stricter, such as his touch making a person and his clothes impure. We cannot use the comparison to make his touch lenient. Only his bedding is lenient, because the פסוק says that directly (Steps 17-19).

keyTerms.meaning: Upon him
To load him, to put a burden on him
It means, it implies

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: a בועל נדה's touch is strict like hers, because 'עליו' makes the comparison a burden. His bedding has only a light impurity, because the פסוק says so directly.

phrases.english: Rava said: "Upon him"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:24, 'ותהי נדתה עליו'.

phrases.english: means to place a burden on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יעקב's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word in the פסוק that sets the direction of the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to her could make his touch lenient like his bedding
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison only adds strictness, so his touch stays strict
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: His touch is strict like hers; only his bedding is light

steps.title: Are all of them really men who live with a נדה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says כותים men are impure because they are בועלי נדות. It asks: is that true of all of them? Some are not married.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] Because they are men who have relations with נדה women, etc. Is that to say that all of them are men who have relations with נדה women?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה about כותים and questions whether it applies to every one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a blanket reason: כותים men are impure because they are בועלי נדות. But an unmarried man does not live with a woman at all. So the reason seems not to fit everyone, and the blanket rule seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: Men who have relations with women who are נדה
Etc.; the rest of the quoted line
Is that to say...? (a question showing surprise)

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] "Because they are men who have relations with niddah women," etc.
Is that to say all of them are men who have relations with niddah women?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן בּוֹעֲלֵי נִדּוֹת וְכוּ׳. אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ בּוֹעֲלֵי נִדּוֹת נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New section: returns to the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's blanket statement that כותים men are בועלי נדות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unmarried men do not live with women, so the reason cannot apply to all of them

steps.title: The משנה means married men only
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק מגדלאה answers that the משנה was speaking only about married כותים men.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק מגדלאה said: They taught this about married women.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק מגדלאה answers the question by narrowing the משנה to married men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in the משנה is not about every כותי man. It covers only men who have wives, because they are the ones assumed to live with a נדה. This keeps the משנה's reason accurate.

keyTerms.meaning: Married women
They taught (this law in the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that כותים men are בועלי נדות applies only to married men.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak of Migdal says:
They taught this about married women.
phrases.notes: He means men who have wives, since they live with a woman whose נדה days they count wrongly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק מַגְדְּלָאָה: בִּנְשׂוּאוֹת שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that all כותים men are בועלי נדות
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means only married כותים men

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: they keep impurity for blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the next words of the משנה, which say that כותים women 'sit on blood,' in order to explain them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they sit for blood,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה. This is a setup line that prepares the ברייתא coming next, which will explain these words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said כותים men count as men who are with a נדה, and gave as the reason that their women 'sit on blood.' At first glance that sounds careful, not careless, so the גמרא needs to explain why it is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'sitting on blood': keeping a seven-day period of impurity because of a sighting of blood
'Etc.': the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: And they sit for blood, etc.
phrases.notes: These are the words of the משנה about כותים women. The full line goes on in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 25-26 explained the first part of the משנה's line, that כותים men are בועלי נדות. Now the גמרא moves on to the next words, the reason the משנה gives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה says כותים women 'sit on blood,' meaning they keep impurity periods because of blood. This phrase now needs explaining.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the problem is finishing the old count after red blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that keeping seven days for each sighting would be fine. The problem is that when red blood comes during a count they began for green blood, they just finish the old count.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי מאיר said: If they kept seven days for each and every sighting of blood, that would be a great fix for them. But what they really do is see red blood and finish it off as part of the count they started for green blood.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר to explain what the משנה means by 'sitting on blood,' and why it makes the כותים women impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Green blood does not make a woman impure, but the כותים start a seven-day count from it anyway. If red blood, which really is impure, comes in the middle, they do not start a new seven days. They just finish the green-blood count, so they end their impurity too early and go to the מקוה while still a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: A great fix: a practice that would keep them safe from sin
Red blood, a color of blood that makes a woman impure
Green blood, a color of blood that does not make a woman impure
They complete: they finish the count they already started

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'strict' here is exactly what causes the problem. By starting a count from pure green blood, they count the red blood's days from the wrong starting point and finish too soon.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הֵן יוֹשְׁבוֹת עַל כׇּל דָּם וָדָם
phrases.english: If they would sit for each and every blood
it would be a great fix for them,
but rather, they see red blood
and complete it toward the green blood.
phrases.notes: They started counting seven days from the green blood, so when red blood comes they just finish that count instead of starting over.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִם הֵן יוֹשְׁבוֹת עַל כׇּל דָּם וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's words quoted in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים women count seven days even from green blood. When red blood comes during that count, they only finish the old count, so they become pure too early.

steps.title: Another explanation: counting the day she stops
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a second reason: a כותית woman counts the day her bleeding stops as the first of her seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: the day on which she stops bleeding, she counts it toward the count of seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a different explanation of why כותים women end up impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זבה must have שבעה נקיים, seven clean days, before she can go to the מקוה. This explanation says the כותים count the very day the bleeding stopped as one of those seven. That would seem to make them finish a day early.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation
The day on which she stops seeing blood
The count of seven clean days a זבה needs

phrases.english: Another explanation: the day on which she stops
phrases.notes: This is about a זבה, a woman who bled several days in a row and must then count seven clean days.

phrases.english: she counts it toward the count of seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different reason for the same משנה, alongside רבי מאיר's reason in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים women count the day the bleeding stops as one of the seven clean days.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: we count that day too
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא challenges the second explanation. Counting the day she stops is normal הלכה, because part of a day counts as the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא challenges this: So let her count it! We also count it, because we hold that part of the day is like the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks the 'other explanation' from step 29. This sets up an answer that the גמרא will need to give next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא argues from the rule מקצת היום ככולו: once the bleeding stops during a day, the rest of that day should count as a clean day. If so, the כותים are right to count it, and we should count it too. So counting the stopping day cannot be the reason the כותים are treated as impure.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it, raising a strong objection
We hold as an accepted rule
Part of the day counts like the whole day

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama challenges this:
So let her count it, and we also would count it,
phrases.notes: 'We' means Jewish women who follow our הלכה.

phrases.english: for we hold that part of the day is like all of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second explanation given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'other explanation' that counting the stopping day makes כותים women impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the rule מקצת היום ככולו, the day the bleeding stops should count as a clean day for us as well. So counting it cannot be what makes the כותים impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge forces the גמרא to show what the כותים really do wrong when they count, which must be different from our normal practice.

steps.title: רבא asks how a seminal emission could ever cancel a day
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the idea that מקצת היום ככולו applies to זיבה. If it did, a seminal emission could never cancel a day of a זב's count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If so, how can you ever have a case where שכבת זרע cancels a day in זיבה? Part of the day counts like the whole day!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רמי בר חמא's claim (Step 30) that part of a day counts as a full day when counting the clean days of זיבה. He brings a known rule that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that if a זב has a seminal emission during his seven clean days, that day is cancelled. But if part of a day counts as a whole day, the clean hours after the emission should still count. So the day would never really be lost, and the rule would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem that follows from someone's claim
Semen; a seminal emission
That cancels (undoes) a day of the seven-day count
The state of a זב or זבה, who must count seven clean days to become pure
Part of the day counts like the whole day

phrases.english: Rava said: If so,
semen, which cancels [a day of the count] in ziva,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in some versions, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording; both mean 'cancels.' He means a זב who has an emission during his seven clean days.

phrases.english: how can you find such a case?
But part of the day is like the whole of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רמי בר חמא's assumption in Step 30 that מקצת היום ככולו applies to זיבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מקצת היום ככולו applies to the seven clean days of זיבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If part of a day counts as whole, a seminal emission could never actually cancel a day. Yet there is an established rule that it does.

steps.title: The rule is about an emission right before sunset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבא: if he saw the emission mid-day, the rest of the day really does count. The rule about cancelling a day is talking about an emission near sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he saw it in the middle of the day, that is true; the rest of the day counts. Here we are dealing with someone who saw it close to sunset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends מקצת היום ככולו by limiting the cancelling rule to one narrow case: an emission right before sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that a mid-day emission would leave enough of the day to count. But near sunset almost no part of the day is left to count. That is the only case where the day is truly lost, so רבא's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle of the day
Indeed, that is so: agreeing with a point
What case are we dealing with here? Introduces a narrower reading of the case
Sunset

phrases.english: If he saw it in the middle of the day,
indeed so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: yes, in that case the rest of the day does count, and he loses nothing.

phrases.english: here, what are we dealing with?
With one who saw it close to sunset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in Step 31 by limiting the cancelling rule to an emission near sunset.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself, not the cancelling rule. The rule still stands, but only for one narrow case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed the rule covers emissions at any time of day. It can be read as referring only to an emission right before sunset, when no part of the day remains to count.

steps.title: Can a whole verse be limited to sunset?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it is reasonable to say that the פסוק teaching this rule was written only about an emission right before sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: And should one get up and say about the פסוק that when it was written, it was written only about an emission close to sunset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 32. The rule comes from a פסוק, and the פסוק gives no hint of such a narrow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for this rule is a פסוק that speaks generally about a seminal emission. Limiting it to the last moments before sunset seems to squeeze a broad פסוק into a very small corner.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק (verse)
It is written
Should one get up and say? Expresses surprise at a forced reading

phrases.english: And should one get up and say about the verse,
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 15:32.

phrases.english: that when it was written,
it was written about close to sunset?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sunset answer of Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the cancelling rule applies only to an emission near sunset.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general פסוק should not be limited to such a rare, narrow case without any sign in the text.

steps.title: Yes, the verse is forced into that narrow case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. We have no choice but to read the פסוק narrowly, because of the rule מקצת היום ככולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. You are forced to set aside the plain reading of the פסוק, because the פסוק itself pushes us to limit it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the narrow reading. It admits the reading is tight, but says there is no other choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If part of a day counts as a whole day, a mid-day emission can never cancel a day. The only time the פסוק's rule can apply is near sunset. So the פסוק itself forces this narrow reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Against your will; by necessity
Leave it aside
It forces itself and sets itself in a narrow case

steps.whatToRemember: According to this approach, מקצת היום ככולו does apply to זיבה. The rule that a seminal emission cancels a day is limited to an emission right before sunset.

phrases.english: Yes, by necessity leave the verse aside,
for it squeezes and establishes itself [in this narrow case].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 33 by accepting the narrow reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts a forced, narrow reading of the פסוק out of necessity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A general פסוק cannot be limited to the last moments before sunset.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since מקצת היום ככולו applies, the פסוק can only work near sunset, so it must be read that way.

steps.title: Does a woman who discharges semen cancel a day of her count?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether a woman who discharges שכבת זרע cancels a day of her זיבה count. He begins to lay out the sides: maybe she counts as one who 'saw' semen, and so she cancels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: A woman who discharges שכבת זרע, does she cancel a day of her זיבה count? Maybe she is like one who 'sees' semen, and so she cancels.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens, following from the rule that semen cancels a day for a זב. The גמרא begins to lay out the first side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who has an emission cancels a day of his count. The question is whether a woman who discharges semen after relations is treated the same way. If she counts as having 'seen' semen herself, she would cancel a day just like him.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who discharges semen after relations
What is the law? Opens a question
She counts as one who 'sees' (has her own emission)

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
A woman who discharges semen,
what is the law: does she cancel [a day] in ziva?
Is she like one who sees, and so she cancels,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule from Step 31 that semen cancels a day for a זב, and asks whether it also applies to a woman who discharges semen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman who discharges semen cancels a day of her seven clean days, and whether that is because she counts as one who 'saw' semen herself.
